title: Adaptive contrast profiles for theme + density switches: audit & VPAT evidence
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Problem: Our component library currently applies a single contrast ramp that assumes the default density and theme. When customers switch to compact density or to high-contrast/dark themes, several controls (buttons, table row actions, chart legends, inline pills) fall below WCAG 2.1 AA thresholds or lose sufficient focus visibility. This ticket scopes an audit and design fixes to introduce adaptive contrast profiles (per-theme, per-density) + produce VPAT evidence artifacts for 508 compliance reviews.
acceptance_criteria: Contrast token mapping exists for default, compact, and high-contrast themes and is documented in the tokens registry
Buttons (primary/secondary/ghost), table row hover/focus states, chart legends, and compact pills pass WCAG AA contrast @ 3:1 for large text and 4.5:1 for normal text where applicable
Focus outlines and keyboard-visible states are preserved or enhanced at all densities and themes (keyboard nav test matrix completed)
Automated visual regression + accessibility checks added to the DS test harness for the new profiles
VPAT-ready evidence pack assembled: token diff docs, screenshots across major components+states, keyboard nav video clips, and testing procedure notes
tasks: Inventory components affected: buttons, pills, compact list items, table rows, chart legends, floating actions
Run automated color-contrast sweeps across themes and density variations (use axe + custom luminance checks)
Design token proposal: create tokens /*contrast.*.density.{default|compact}*/ per theme, include semantic naming and usage guidance
Prototype CSS variables & component-level overrides for compact density to avoid token explosion
Developer handoff: create GH PR with token changes and component updates; include Percy snapshots and axe checks
Coordinate with QA to add keyboard nav scenarios to E2E suite (tab order, roving tabindex cases)
Assemble VPAT evidence folder and draft VPAT language for legal/compliance review
comments: 2026-02-11 Maya Thompson: Kickoff meeting notes added to Confluence. Agreed to treat compact density as a first-class variant rather than ad-hoc overrides.

2026-03-03 Design Review: PM sign-off on semantic token names; asked to include accessibility rationale in each token description for VPAT reviewers.
2026-03-08 QA: Added keyboard nav scenarios to Cypress E2E; initial run flagged focus outline clipping on virtualized table rows in compact mode.

notes: Trade-offs: aggressive contrast increases can visually dominate UI and reduce perceived depth. We will prioritize text/interactive affordances and use elevation/opacity for non-text visual balance.
Risk: legacy customer themes may rely on current tokens; include migration notes and a compatibility guide in the release docs.
Follow-up: After merge, schedule a 2-week monitoring window to collect console and support tickets related to visual regressions.
